The inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs also exists for other requirements, e.g., MOP, OoBB, Narrow band blocking and etc, and RAN5 spec does not consider the inconsistencies for other requirements except spurious emission for UE co-existence. Currently most of the new UEs under testing in test labs are still R15 UEs, and only a few of them are R16 UEs. If RAN5 spec considers the inconsistencies between Releases in RAN4 specs, more and more UEs will be blocked to enter certain country or region’s market as they will cause unacceptable interference to co-existing systems, and the n50 and n78 R15 UEs have to meet some unnecessary spurious emission requirements for protected bands that have been recognized as not necessary. It is more serious for LTE as currently new LTE UEs under testing in test labs can be of any release from Rel-8 to Rel-16, and most of them are Rel-15 or backward (e.g., Rel-9, Rel-10, Rel-11, Rel-12. Rel-13, Rel-15). Bands are Release independent in 3GPP, and RAN5 only maintain one Release of spec. Just as what MOP, OoBB, Narrow band blocking and other test cases have done, Spurious emission for UE co-existence test case does not need to include Release information in minimum requirements and test requirements. Proposal 2: RAN5 shall take the latest Release of RAN4 spec as reference for the requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence and remove the Release information in minimum requirements and test requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence. New bands/new CBWs/or new PCs introduced to later Releases can be excluded if there is no interested operator in RAN5. Proposal 3: Minimum requirements and test requirements of Spurious emission for UE co-existence in TS 38.521-1/-2/-3 and TS 36.521-1 shall be updated as per Proposal 1 and Proposal 2.

Title: Aligning the tabular representation of ASN.1 with PRD13 sections 4.8 and 5 Reason for change: RAN5 has agreed rules for tabular representation in RAN5 specs of the RRC messages specified in ASN.1 in RAN5 specs (e.g. TS 38.331). These rules are defined in RAN5 PRD13 and have been applied since the introduction of the LTE Conformance testing. However, some of these rules have not been applied consistently when 5G RRC messages have been specified in TS 38.508-1. This from one side lowers the quality of the RAN5 specs but from another provides room for confusion and misinterpretation of the RRC messages definitions. RAN5 raised an AP#86.03 calling for a solution. Examples of rules which have not been followed: (1) The conversion into a tabular format of the ASN.1 definitions for SEQUENCE OF TYPE where the TYPE is a locally or externally defined User defined ASN.1 type for example drb-CountMSB-InfoList SEQUENCE (SIZE (1..maxDRB)) OF DRB-CountMSB-Info, where DRB-CountMSB-Info itself is defined as DRB-CountMSB-Info SEQUENCE (2) The ASN.1 symbol "::=" shall be used only at the very top level of the element definition (on the parent name) and not in the definition of the sub-fields (3) Indentation rules for sub-elements (4) Groups of elements shall be identified by enclosing them between brackets { ... } (5) Invisible rows borders for elements with multiple alternative values (6) No need for type definition for elements which are set to 'Not Present' Other issues found: redundant spaces, paragraphs, spec TS 38.508-1 referred to from TS 38.508-1, non 3GPP styles. Summary of change: Corrections have been applied throughout the spec to align the messages definitions with the RAN5 agreed rules for tabular representation in RAN5 specs of the RRC messages specified in ASN.1. Editorial error repaired. Consequences if not approved: Low quality of RAN5 specs. Inconsistency. Differences between the representation on the prose and the implementation in TTCN. Possibility for misinterpretation of the required content of RRC messages which can lead to compliant devices being unfairly failed during testing, or/and, non-compliant devices passing the tests. Clauses affected: 4.6, 4.8.1, 4.9.12A, 4.9.12B, 4.9.17, 4.9.18, 5.4, 5.5
